wording: Faroese domestic full liability arises from a home under Tax Act §1(1)(1), or, without a home, a stay of at least **180 days in a twelve-month period**, interrupted or not, under §1(1)(4). Exactly 180 meets that stay test; fewer days do not disprove the separate home test. Other statutory routes include specified students/apprentices abroad and seafarers. Determine commencement/cessation and treaty residence separately. Fully liable persons start with worldwide income under §25; nonresidents are limited to §2 categories. [Tax Act §§1–2, 25][tax]

wording: For business profit, reconcile sales and expenses, remove private withdrawals/use, correct inventory and replace accounting depreciation with the statutory asset schedule. Section 31 permits expenses incurred to earn, secure and maintain business income but expressly excludes ordinary expenses of earning A-income/personal employment income. Do not deduct an employee's ordinary work costs as sole-trader costs. Business interest/finance costs follow §33(1)(1), including its unpaid-interest clawback. Pre-trading research expenditure has the separate §32 start-year/next-three-years rule. Carry business losses under §33a only when not usable earlier; debt-release loss reductions must be applied. [Tax Act §§26, 31–33a][tax]

wording: Before finalising an individual's depreciation or investment-fund deduction, apply Tax Act §31(2)–(6)'s separate **personal-consumption floor**. If taxable income is below the statutory consumption computation, increase income toward that amount, but by no more than the depreciation/investment-fund deductions covered by the rule. Section 31(4) excludes year-bound depreciation that would otherwise be lost. Under §31(5), the denied depreciation is treated as not taken in that year; preserve it in the asset records instead of losing it or deducting it twice. For spouses, the statutory consumption calculation includes both spouses' full-year income and opening/closing assets and liabilities. This floor is distinct from an asset's private-use adjustment. Obtain the actual consumption working paper before confirming the base. [Tax Act §31(2)–(6)][tax]

section: ### 2. Sole trader, child credit and private investments
wording: Assume a full-year eligible non-church Tórshavnar resident, with DKK 600,000 business revenue, DKK 260,000 deductible non-private costs, and an ordinary exclusive-business opening equipment pool DKK 200,000 with no additions/disposals. Electing 30% depreciation gives DKK 60,000. An independently eligible DKK 40,000 pension payment made in 2026 is deducted once, leaving ordinary income DKK 240,000. Assume the independently verified statutory personal-consumption computation is DKK 200,000, so the §31 floor requires no increase; this is a case input, not a statutory fixed allowance. The resident is the sole eligible recipient of the full-year credits for one child aged five on 1 January. National tax DKK 23,950 less DKK 10,700 credit is DKK 13,250; municipal DKK 39,900 less DKK 9,000 is DKK 30,900. Separate non-business share gains DKK 40,000, fully eligible share loss DKK 5,000 and bank interest DKK 5,000 give DKK 40,000 capital net gain and DKK 14,000 capital tax. Combined ordinary/capital income tax is DKK 58,150, before withholding credits. Pension contribution tax and social charges are separate. Assume no prior capital losses, foreign credit, private-use adjustment, special regime or other deduction.
